decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach: left toward cameras, right toward right-side objects. Raise and tilt gradually; category assignment will use current RGB.
Approach first left camera and right rabbit from above, keeping arms separated and grippers open; refine grasp from wrist views.
Fine-align above camera and rabbit using wrist images; descend cautiously with nearly vertical approach before closing.
Close on first camera and right rabbit after a short descent, then test retention with a small vertical lift.
RGB indicates both objects retained. Lift clear and carry camera toward white basket, rabbit toward blue basket; keep both grippers closed.
Replan after rejected suffix with smaller increments and lower transport height. Carry retained camera and rabbit over their separate baskets without crossing arms.
Both held objects are over their baskets. Lower and release the camera into white and rabbit into blue; avoid further forward extension of the right arm.
Withdraw from released objects and approach second left camera and rightmost watch. Rotate left jaws to align with the camera's short dimension.
Visually refine second-camera and watch alignment, descending in small increments with open jaws.
Close and test-lift the aligned second camera. Center the right watch between open jaws and descend gently.
Camera appears retained; lift and start toward white basket. Correct the watch slightly left, close, and test retention with a small lift.
Transport retained camera over white basket. Watch was not retained; reopen, recenter on its new position and approach lower to engage the band.
Place and release second camera fully inside white. Shift right grasp back over the watch band, close and test with a short lift.
Cameras released in white; withdraw left toward remaining rabbit while restoring jaw orientation. Lift retained watch and carry toward red basket with gripper closed.
Align left over remaining rabbit with open jaws. Raise right watch above basket rim before advancing into red.
Grasp and test-lift remaining rabbit. Move retained watch deeper into red before lowering. A camera is visible outside white's front edge and will need recovery.
Lower and release watch over red. Carry retained rabbit toward blue, tilting slightly forward to reduce reach demand while maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Advance rabbit over left half of blue while retaining it. Withdraw open right gripper from the released watch and keep the arms separated.
Release second rabbit inside blue, then withdraw left toward the displaced camera. Park right near its side of the center for later watch transfers.
Both rabbits appear in blue. Approach displaced camera in front of white for recovery; right remains clear on its side.
Refine recovery grasp from wrist view: move left and forward toward the camera, descending slowly with open jaws.
Center the displaced camera between left jaws, close, then lift slightly to verify retention before repositioning.
Camera appears retained. Lift well above white basket rim, then advance while tilting forward to place it deeper without extending the arm excessively.
Lower recovered camera farther inside white and release. Keep right stationary until the left placement settles.
Cameras now appear inside white. Withdraw and approach the black watch; remaining left-side watches will be staged centrally for right-arm delivery to red without crossing arms.
Align the black watch's band between left jaws and descend cautiously. Right remains clear for the later central transfer.
Fine-center on black watch, close around its band and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Black watch appears retained. Lift and stage it at the workspace boundary for right-arm pickup, keeping the left EE on the left and right arm stationary.
Lower black watch onto the central tabletop and release for sequential pickup. Keep the left EE left of center; right waits until left withdraws.
Withdraw left from the staged black watch toward the remaining silver watch. Once clear, right approaches black from its own side of center.
Refine separate watch approaches: left forward onto silver band, right slightly left and forward onto staged black band; keep both EEs in their own workspaces.
Close around both aligned watch bands after final small descents; test-lift and begin moving the right watch away from the central pickup area.
Carry retained black watch toward red. Test the uncertain silver-band grasp with a vertical lift before attempting its transfer.
Silver watch was not retained; reopen and approach lower. Carry black watch farther inside red while tilting forward to preserve reach margin.
Correct silver grasp backward to center the band at jaw contact depth, then close and test. Lower and release black watch inside red.
Silver band now appears retained. Lift and carry it to the central staging spot; withdraw right from the two watches released in red, keeping arms separated.
Lower and release the final watch onto the central staging area. Reorient right for pickup while it stays clear of the left gripper.
Withdraw the left arm fully from the staged watch before bringing the right arm toward it, keeping both EEs on their own side of center.
Return left toward origin. Right approaches the staged watch from its side of center with a slight inward tilt and a cautious descent.
Finish left return to origin. Close right around the final watch band after a small descent, then test retention with a vertical lift.
Final watch does not appear securely retained. Reopen and approach the band lower and slightly backward; left stays at origin.
Close on the recentered silver band, then lift vertically to verify that the watch follows the right gripper.
The silver watch slipped and flipped on the table. Reopen and recenter over its new position, approaching lower for a more secure grasp.
Attempt a lower grasp on the silver watch case rather than the loose band, then test retention with a small lift.
Test whether the narrow band is retained with a higher lift and small rightward transport; keep the gripper closed and left at origin.
Watch remained on the table. Reopen and approach its latest position farther backward, aiming to enclose the solid case rather than pinching an empty portion of the ring.
Descend more deeply around the tilted watch case before closing; earlier attempts appear to have closed above the useful gripping surface.
Lift vertically from the latest observed pose with the right gripper closed to assess whether the deeper case grasp retains the watch.
The watch now appears suspended from the closed jaws. Lift clear and carry toward red with a slight forward tilt, monitoring retention.
Carry the visibly retained final watch over red, maintaining a forward tilt and closed jaws until fully inside the basket.
Release final watch inside red with minimal drop, allow settling, then lift and withdraw the open right gripper clear of the basket.
All objects appear grouped in their baskets. Return the open right arm toward origin along a continuous elbow-up path while allowing the watches to settle.
